text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today as oil prices weakened following the G7's announcement to release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over the next four months. That supply injection, intended to ease fuel shortages tied to Middle East and Europe conflicts, typically weighs on crude prices in the near term—and with U.S. oil trading around $96 per barrel today versus higher levels earlier this week, the stock reflected that downward pressure.

The two-week decline of nearly 4% sits within the normal volatility for an oil major reacting to shifting geopolitical risk and energy supply dynamics. While tensions in the Middle East (U.S. carrier deployments, potential Iran strikes) can support oil prices, the immediate news flow today centered on supply relief rather than disruption risk, which is why the stock drifted lower despite the broader uncertainty.
